newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close off, slip with bonds and U.S..
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close off, slip with bonds and U.S..

text.p: Most Dutch shares ended sharply lower on Thursday, the first trading day of the new year, with the main share index losing 13.83 points to close at 634.41.

Pressured at the opening by Wall Street's lower close, Dutch blue chips continued to trade nervously, negatively influenced by other European bourses and the domestic bond market. After New York headed south again, Amsterdam lost further ground.
Dealers said today's correction was justified, as the recent rise of Dutch stocks had been based upon very thin trade.

"The market just kept on rising, without any fundamental basis. Now, with a lower Wall Street and inflation fears rising again, there is a reason for stocks to fall. I think we will go down some more points," one dealer said.
He said recent corrections had all been too small and were too brief, adding the market needed a five percent fall to trigger large-scale buying again.
Insurer Aegon, boosted by its deal with U.S. Providian Corp announced on Monday, slipped at the end of the day, following its fellow financial stocks and the bond market.

Retail was the only winning sector, with dealers happy to see the Dutch October consumer spending rise 5.1 percent on an annual basis. Retailer De Boer was up 3.10 guilders at 124.60, Gamma gained 2.50 at 85.90, while Vendex ended 1.20 higher at 75.10 guilders.
Ahold ended off three guilders at 105.00 after its 73 percent owned wholesaler Schuitema released a 4.1 percent sales growth figure for 1996.
Dealers expect bourse turnover to remain thin until the start of next week, when all parties will return to the market.
"We have to get started, see what our positions are, decide upon the strategy...Once that's done, things will get going again," one dealer said.
